title: The custom chip driving Waymo’s robotaxi ambitions
summary: Waymo has developed a custom 5 nm ASIC chip to enhance the performance and efficiency of its sixth-generation self-driving system, used in its Ojai robotaxi. The chip delivers over 1,000 TOPS of computing power, enabling faster and safer reactions in complex urban environments. This vertical integration is key to reducing costs and improving scalability for Waymo’s autonomous vehicle operations.
key_points: Waymo’s custom 5 nm ASIC chip is designed to process raw data from 13 high-fidelity cameras before it reaches the core self-driving system.
The chip delivers over 1,000 TOPS of computing performance, comparable to Nvidia’s DRIVE AGX Thor.
This custom silicon improves efficiency and performance, critical for safe operations in high-density urban areas.
Waymo’s vertical integration includes partnerships with AMD, Micron, Nvidia, Samsung, Sandisk, Socionext, and TSMC.
The chip is part of Waymo’s strategy to reduce costs and scale its robotaxi service profitably.
